subject: Service diversion notice and post-incident check-in — ShopStream
messages:
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: ops-eng@shopstream.com, sanjay.k@shopstream.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate: service diversion applied for ShopStream (eu-west) — guidance and next steps

Hi Sanjay / ShopStream ops team,

Update from Redwood: we detected elevated 5xx rates and request timeouts affecting customers routed through the eu-west cloud region beginning ~2028-06-30T08:45Z. Automatic diversion to a cold-standby pool in eu-central was applied at 08:58Z; we also enabled cross-region routing to the us-west pool for any fallbacks that exceeded latency thresholds.

Impact summary:
- Affected paths: inference endpoints (text-generation and embeddings) for eu-west and customers pinned to eu-west.
- Symptoms: increased 5xx, higher p50/p95 latency for certain long-context requests.
- Current status: majority of traffic redirected; API token auth and data plane unchanged.

Immediate guidance for you (short checklist):
1) If you have region pinning enabled, set region=eu-central or region=us-west in your SDK calls to avoid hitting eu-west until we clear. Example: region param or X-Redwood-Region header.
2) Avoid model upgrades during the window — use the pinned model version (v20280615-quant) until we confirm recovery.
3) If you have strict data residency restrictions, reply to this thread immediately; we'll coordinate options (VPC private route or dedicated pool).

Attachments: fallback-config.json (sample request overrides), customer-reroute-steps.txt (ordered steps and curl examples).

We will follow up with a post-incident summary and a link to the full timeline. For now, please confirm whether the temporary region=eu-central setting is acceptable for your workload.

— Olga

Subject: Post-incident update: eu-west diversion removed; summary + next steps

Hi Sanjay / ShopStream team — follow-up with the actions we completed and what to expect next. Thanks for your patience.

Executive summary:
- Root cause: a misconfiguration in a peering route between our eu-west cloud provider edge and the eu-west inference subnets caused packet drops for long-lived gRPC streams under specific multi-tenant load patterns.
- Mitigation applied: automated reroute + temporary cold-standby activation in eu-central at 08:58Z, and limited cross-region failover to us-west for saturated paths. eu-west was restored to normal routing at 11:05Z after peering rule rollback and targeted kernel patch.
- Impact window: 08:45Z — 11:05Z (approx).

Actions we've taken for ShopStream:
1) We left eu-central as the recommended temporary region while we validate BGP peering stability. You can set region=eu-central in client calls; that pool remains within EU boundaries (no egress to non-EU regions).
2) We validated model parity for v20280615-quant across eu-central and eu-west; inference outputs are consistent within normal nondeterminism bounds.
3) Ops & Legal: If you require a dedicated EU-only VPC or a contractual addendum, open a support case with enterprise-support@redwood.ai and reference DEAL-9321.

Attachments: incident_timeline.pdf (detailed timeline), fallback-config.json, customer-reroute-steps.txt.

Postmortem link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-incident-postmortem-shopstream (contains RCA, telemetry charts, and remediation plan).

SLA/credits: we will follow our documented SLA process. Monica, can you own a short credits instruction doc and an intake link for ShopStream? Expect a separate email with steps by end of day.

Next steps we propose with you:
- Short sync w/ ShopStream ops next 48 hours to validate traffic patterns after the reroute (30 min). Please suggest times.
- Weekly check-ins for two weeks if you prefer to monitor behavior.

Please reply to confirm whether you accept eu-central as the temporary region and whether you'd like the 30-min sync tomorrow.

— Olga
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
